qs.q:
Making Films — Which person…

A=Abigail (used to criticise films; tried short filmmaking; thought it would be easy; in retrospect very wrong; produced acclaimed documentaries for a time)
B=Bert (pitched in acting for John's films; developed passion for film history; studied film; post-production is most complex; audience reception is key)
C=Connie (good story, great team, did well at box office; yet didn't meet personal expectations; realised success depends on timing and many factors)
D=David (project management helps; ultimate fate determined by aesthetics, creative imagery, sound; respects filmmakers greatly; considers it well-deserved though hard)
E=Emma (five key phases; films inexplicably fail despite meeting expectations; important to have a fully rounded author vision from the start)
F=Francis (passion and pressure create good films; fear at start is natural; must plan journey first: locations, permits, crew, budget; leads to streamlined post-production)

0. created documentaries in the course of their career? [A=Abigail]
1. claims that the most demanding part of creating a film is in the post-production phase?
2. says they created a film that came short of their professional expectations?
3. states that a film will be successful if you know exactly what you want your film to achieve from the start?
4. believes that not connecting with the audience can be detrimental to a film?
5. says the success of a film depends on when you bring together and how you balance different aspects of filmmaking?
6. admits they have enjoyed a limited period of success working in the film industry?
7. argues that a filmmaker won't succeed if they don't have a strong artistic background?
8. states they enjoyed the support of the experts they gathered for the project?
9. says that the filmmaker's final product justifies the money they are making?
10. finds that being well-organised initially can tip the scale of success in the later stages of filmmaking?
11. mentions that, based on their experience, creating a film can be a strenuous process?
12. suggests that you need to be passionate about your filmmaking project to succeed?
items: 1 — claims the most demanding part is in the post-production phase?
2 — says they created a film that came short of their professional expectations?
3 — states that a film will be successful if you know exactly what you want your film to achieve from the start?
4 — believes that not connecting with the audience can be detrimental to a film?
5 — says the success of a film depends on when you bring together and how you balance different aspects?
6 — admits they have enjoyed a limited period of success working in the film industry?
7 — argues that a filmmaker won't succeed if they don't have a strong artistic background?
8 — states they enjoyed the support of the experts they gathered for the project?
9 — says that the filmmaker's final product justifies the money they are making?
10 — finds that being well-organised initially can tip the scale of success in the later stages?
11 — mentions that, based on their experience, creating a film can be a strenuous process?
12 — suggests that you need to be passionate about your filmmaking project to succeed?

qs.q:
Crop Circles – Messages in the Fields

"Elaborate motifs, often tens of metres across... 'Crop circles' were CONCENTRATED IN AREAS OF ENGLAND CLOSE TO ANCIENT ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITES like Stonehenge and the Avebury Stone Circle."

The crop circles were known to be…
A the work of alien cultures.
B arranged in complex patterns.
C at sites of archaeological interest.
D made by farmers seeking publicity.

Crop Circles

"Although the crops would ALWAYS SPRING BACK INTACT to their previous position."

One thing that the crop circles did NOT cause was…
A physical damage to plants.
B an increase in legal consultations.
C an upsurge of interest in unidentified flying objects.
D confrontations between landowners and unwelcome visitors.
opts: an upsurge of interest in unidentified flying objects.
confrontations between landowners and unwelcome visitors.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"The mystery about their origins provided THE IDEAL OPPORTUNITY FOR NEWSPAPER EDITORS. They SEIZED ON THE REGULAR OPPORTUNITIES for writing extensive articles featuring stunning aerial photographs."

According to the author, those who benefited most from crop circles were…
A local people.
B new-age travellers.
C newspaper editors.
D Doug Bower and Dave Chorley.

Crop Circles

"Fields of wheat and corn had become ARENAS OF CONFLICT during the historic miners' strike... there were VIOLENT CONFRONTATIONS BETWEEN POLICE AND NEW-AGE TRAVELLERS... the RAVE CULTURE of pop-up open-air dance parties was getting under way."

The author draws particular attention to fields as…
A sites of particular historic interest.
B places inhabited by sun-worshippers.
C significant, in the broader sense, to agriculture.
D places characterised by frequent public disturbances.
opts: significant, in the broader sense, to agriculture.
places characterised by frequent public disturbances.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"These cheeky exploits... were eccentric expressions of RESISTANCE to the increasing concentration of English land in the hands of financiers... can be seen as A FURTHER BLOSSOMING OF LAND-BASED ART by practitioners ranging from Andy Goldsworthy to Banksy."

The article describes crop circles as…
A saying nothing at all.
B keeping a pact of secrecy.
C focusing attention on investments.
D extending the repertoire of artistic expression.
opts: extending the repertoire of artistic expression.

qs.q:
Crop Circles

"It COULD NEVER BE MONETISED, and this is why... what remains is simply a TRADITION OF GREAT ART."

According to the author, it was impossible to exploit crop circles because they…
A were not permanent.
B could not be exhibited.
C were made anonymously.
D were associated with the rave culture.
opts: were associated with the rave culture.

How to Stop Overthinking

"Sometimes we can find ourselves stuck in repetitive, unhelpful thought patterns that make us feel overwhelmed. (19) ____. Also, other areas of our lives can be affected, as well as our relationships."

A Like any new positive behaviour that you undertake, they take time and practice.
B When we are focused on the present moment, we are not contemplating the past or worrying about the future.
C Exercise, take part in a conversation, watch a show you love, or work on another project.
D This can negatively impact our mood and, ultimately, how we work.
E If it is still a concern, then you can proceed to problem solving.
F Acknowledge the negative aspects and then evaluate if there are other ways to think about it.
G It results in us making assumptions about what was meant by their comment, or reading between the lines.
H Instead of asking why something happened, ask if there is an answer to the problem.
opts: A — They take time and practice.
B — When focused on the present moment, we are not contemplating the past.
C — Exercise, take part in a conversation, watch a show, or work on another project.
D — This can negatively impact our mood and, ultimately, how we work.
E — If it is still a concern, then you can proceed to problem solving.
F — Acknowledge the negative aspects and evaluate if there are other ways to think about it.
G — It results in us making assumptions about what was meant by their comment.
H — Instead of asking why something happened, ask if there is an answer.
